emb:L2038530778.model_family: texture analysis combined with machine learning
emb:L2038530778.clinical_problem: assessment of renal function and detection of scarring in chronic kidney disease
emb:L2038530778.model_description: This narrative overview describes renal scintigraphy as the main imaging test for kidney function in children, capable of detecting parenchymal scarring and predicting progression of chronic kidney disease. It discusses how texture analysis of the images can be combined with machine learning to quantify renal tissue heterogeneity as an additional predictive tool, without describing a specific trained model or dataset.

emb:L2038673893.clinical_problem: low-dose chest CT image quality for congenital heart disease imaging
emb:L2038673893.patient_population: infants with congenital heart disease undergoing chest CT
emb:L2038673893.model_description: This prospective study compared an AI-based iterative reconstruction algorithm (AIIR) with conventional hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR) for low-dose chest CT in infants with congenital heart disease. Low-dose scans reconstructed with AIIR were compared subjectively and objectively against low-dose HIR images and conventional-dose HIR images. AIIR-reconstructed low-dose images matched the image quality of conventional-dose images while lowering the effective dose.
emb:L2038673893.headline_result: Subjective scores of low-dose AIIR images did not differ from conventional-dose HIR images (most comparisons P>0.05); effective dose fell from 0.85 mSv (conventional) to 0.09 mSv (low-dose).

emb:L2038929833.model_family: Spider Wasp Optimization (SWO) feature selection combined with K-Nearest Neighbor classifier, using features from a ResNet50V2 residual learning architecture
emb:L2038929833.clinical_problem: classification of pediatric brain tumor type
emb:L2038929833.patient_population: pediatric patients with brain tumors (brain MRI from King Abdullah Hospital)
emb:L2038929833.model_description: The model classifies pediatric brain tumor type from MRI images. Features are extracted with a ResNet50V2 deep learning architecture, then a Spider Wasp Optimization metaheuristic algorithm selects the most informative features, which are fed into a K-Nearest Neighbor classifier for binary and multiclass tumor classification. It was compared against other deep learning architectures (MobileNetV2, ResNet50V2) and machine learning classifiers (KNN, SVM, Random Forest).
emb:L2038929833.dataset_size: brain MRI images from King Abdullah Hospital (exact n not stated)
emb:L2038929833.headline_result: SWO+KNN achieved 97.5% accuracy for binary classification and 95.5% for multiclass classification, outperforming other deep learning and machine learning models compared.
emb:L2038929833.study_design: retrospective single-center diagnostic accuracy / technical development

emb:L2039111789.clinical_problem: quantifying spinal deformity severity in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
emb:L2039111789.model_description: The uAI DR scoliosis analysis system automatically measures multiple spinal alignment parameters (Cobb angle, coronal balance distance, T1 slope, pelvic tilt, sacral slope, apical vertebral translation, thoracic trunk shift, thoracic kyphosis, sagittal vertical axis) from anteroposterior and lateral spinal radiographs. The study correlated these AI-measured parameters with AIS severity and coronal/sagittal balance status in a large retrospective cohort.
emb:L2039111789.release_evidence: Parameters were measured using the named 'uAI DR scoliosis analysis System' software product.
emb:L2039111789.headline_result: Cobb angle, coronal balance distance, apical vertebral translation and thoracic trunk shift increased significantly with AIS severity (all P<0.001); T1 slope, apical vertebral translation and thoracic trunk shift were independent predictors of severity.

emb:L2040409059.exclusion_reason: general historical/technology review of prenatal ultrasound in China over 40 years; AI is only a brief forward-looking mention, not the subject of a specific model or study

emb:L2040416928.exclusion_reason: review of domestic CT scanner hardware and low-dose scanning protocols for pediatric CT; AI is mentioned only as a future combination, no AI model developed or evaluated

emb:L2040608424.model_family: AI algorithm for fetal echocardiography (zone detection, view classification, pathology detection)
emb:L2040608424.clinical_problem: screening for congenital heart disease on fetal echocardiography
emb:L2040608424.patient_population: fetuses at 18-21 weeks gestation undergoing fetal echocardiography
emb:L2040608424.model_description: An AI algorithm was developed to support fetal heart examination from five standard cardiac ultrasound video projections (at least 25 frames per slice). The pipeline localizes the fetal chest and heart, classifies which standard heart view a frame shows, and flags whether the heart structure on that slice appears normal or abnormal, producing a 'normal' or 'not normal' (possible CHD, recommend extended echocardiography) opinion. Results were verified against expert diagnosis and postnatal confirmation.
emb:L2040608424.dataset_size: not stated (cases from Moscow Kulakov National Medical Research Center)
emb:L2040608424.headline_result: Accuracy was 98% for locating the chest/heart zone, 82% for classifying the cardiac view, and 77% for detecting pathology on a slice.

emb:L2040720720.exclusion_reason: narrative review of prenatal ultrasound diagnosis of fetal aortic coarctation; AI is mentioned only as a supportive adjunct alongside multiparameter models, not itself developed or evaluated

emb:L2040720990.exclusion_reason: broad review of AI across obstetric practice (preterm birth, gestational diabetes, preeclampsia prediction, fetal heart-rate monitoring); imaging (ultrasound anomaly recognition) is only one of many non-imaging topics covered, not the focus

emb:L2040755738.model_family: deep learning-based multi-view fusion recognition model
emb:L2040755738.clinical_problem: prenatal diagnosis of fetal conotruncal defects
emb:L2040755738.patient_population: fetuses at 20-32 weeks gestation with suspected conotruncal defects and matched normal controls
emb:L2040755738.model_description: A deep learning model takes one standard image each from four fetal cardiac ultrasound views (four-chamber, left ventricular outflow tract, right ventricular outflow tract, three vessels and trachea) and fuses them to classify the conotruncal anatomy as normal or defective. Three fusion strategies requiring positivity on two, three, or four views were compared; the best model was validated against post-abortion pathology or postnatal echocardiography and against sonologists of varying experience.
emb:L2040755738.dataset_size: 88 CTD cases and 176 controls (82 CTD and 161 controls after exclusions); 60/22 CTD and 120/41 control train/validation split
emb:L2040755738.headline_result: Optimal fusion model (Fusion Model 1) had 86% sensitivity and 76% specificity, statistically comparable to senior sonologists (91%, P>0.999) and significantly better than intermediate (55%, P=0.049) and junior sonologists (32%, P=0.003).

emb:L2040762543.exclusion_reason: pediatric relevance is only background framing ('particularly in children under five'); the study population and dataset age are not stated, so pediatric involvement cannot be confirmed

emb:L2041738076.clinical_problem: improving diagnostic accuracy and efficiency of pediatric ultrasound interpretation
emb:L2041738076.model_description: This review summarizes recent AI applications across pediatric ultrasound subspecialties, covering preliminary diagnosis, screening, detailed image analysis, and clinical decision support. It discusses how AI can improve structural recognition and provide automated, standardized measurements to address operator dependence and inconsistent image quality inherent to pediatric ultrasound, and assist less-experienced physicians.

emb:L2042120231.model_family: radiomic quantitative parameters (Dmax/DmaxVox) extracted with LIFEx software and manual measurement
emb:L2042120231.clinical_problem: prognostic risk stratification in pediatric Hodgkin lymphoma
emb:L2042120231.patient_population: pediatric patients with newly diagnosed Hodgkin lymphoma undergoing baseline and interim 18F-FDG PET/CT
emb:L2042120231.model_description: Two novel quantitative PET/CT parameters, Dmax and DmaxVox (the distance between the two most distant hypermetabolic foci or voxels within a lesion), were measured on baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT using the LIFEx software and by manual measurement, then normalized to body surface area or height. The normalized values were tested for association with event-free survival in children with Hodgkin lymphoma.
emb:L2042120231.headline_result: Height-normalized SDmaxVox was significantly associated with event-free survival (P=0.03); negative predictive value exceeded 95% for both LIFEx- and manually-derived SDmaxVox at optimal cut-offs (0.123 and 0.086).

emb:L2044159236.clinical_problem: prenatal screening and diagnosis of congenital heart disease
emb:L2044159236.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal cardiac ultrasound screening
emb:L2044159236.model_description: This review summarizes progress in applying AI to prenatal ultrasound for congenital heart disease, including recognition of standard fetal cardiac ultrasound planes, segmentation of cardiac anatomical structures, and screening/diagnosis of complex CHD, along with the clinical challenges limiting adoption.

emb:L2044159248.clinical_problem: standardized identification of prenatal ultrasound screening planes
emb:L2044159248.model_description: A VMamba-based model was trained to automatically recognize 21 standard prenatal ultrasound screening planes/sections from 2D images. Its classification performance was compared against ResNet-50, Swin-Transformer, ConvNeXtV2, RepViT, and MSPANet, with Grad-CAM heat maps and t-SNE plots used to check whether the model attended to the correct anatomical structures.
emb:L2044159248.headline_result: VMamba achieved the best performance among compared models: sensitivity 94.54%, specificity 99.72%, accuracy 94.42%, AUC 0.997, F1 0.944.

emb:L2044159638.exclusion_reason: evaluates a training method for physician trainees using an AI ultrasound workstation as an educational aid; it measures trainee skill acquisition, not an imaging AI model's diagnostic performance in patients

emb:L2044159656.clinical_problem: prenatal diagnosis of fetal ocular malformations
emb:L2044159656.patient_population: fetuses with prenatally screened ocular malformations and normal controls
emb:L2044159656.model_description: A Swin-Transformer-based model was trained on fetal ophthalmic ultrasound images to distinguish normal fetal eyes from ocular malformations. Its diagnostic performance was compared against MobileNet-V2, ResNet-50, VGG-16 and Vision-Transformer models, with heat maps and confusion-matrix/t-SNE analysis used to assess interpretability.
emb:L2044159656.dataset_size: 1,282 ophthalmic ultrasound images of malformed fetal eyes and 526 images of normal fetal eyes (8:1:1 train/validation/test split)
emb:L2044159656.headline_result: The Swin-Transformer model achieved sensitivity 88.31%, specificity 97.37%, AUC 0.990, precision 87.31%, F1 87.71% in the test set, outperforming the four comparison models.

emb:L2044839923.exclusion_reason: review of genetic counseling practice in obstetrics (chromosomal/single-gene disorders, NIPT, ethics); AI is mentioned only briefly regarding non-imaging polygenic risk scoring

emb:L2045854623.clinical_problem: use of AI to support point-of-care ultrasound in pediatric emergency and critical care
emb:L2045854623.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing point-of-care ultrasound in emergency and critical care settings
emb:L2045854623.model_description: This review assesses the advantages and limitations of AI-assisted point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in pediatrics. It reports that AI-assisted models can improve image acquisition and diagnostic accuracy, particularly for less-experienced users, and can augment training in settings with limited ultrasound expertise, while cautioning that most models are trained on adult data and need pediatric-specific validation before use.

emb:L2036750800.exclusion_reason: adult hepatocellular carcinoma cohort undergoing CT radiomics analysis; no pediatric population

emb:L2037149829.model_family: machine learning brain-age estimation models (structural/functional/morphometric connectome features)
emb:L2037149829.clinical_problem: brain developmental deviation (brain age gap) as a biomarker in early-onset schizophrenia
emb:L2037149829.patient_population: antipsychotic-naive first-episode early-onset schizophrenia patients (childhood and adolescence) and typically developing controls
emb:L2037149829.model_description: Structural (T1-weighted, diffusion) and functional resting-state MRI were used to build three connectome types (morphometric similarity, structural, functional) in youths with early-onset schizophrenia and typically developing controls. Eight brain-age estimation models were trained on the control group's connectome features, and the best model was applied to estimate each patient's brain age; the gap between estimated and chronological age was compared between groups and correlated with symptom severity.
emb:L2037149829.dataset_size: 80 early-onset schizophrenia patients and 91 typically developing controls
emb:L2037149829.headline_result: Structural and morphometric-similarity connectome features gave the best brain-age estimates; EOS patients had widened structural brain-age gaps that differed between childhood and adolescence and correlated positively with clinical symptom severity.

emb:L2036664225.model_family: radiomics-based binary classification model (ANOVA feature selection, ten-fold cross-validation)
emb:L2036664225.clinical_problem: prediction of motor neurodevelopmental outcome in preterm infants
emb:L2036664225.patient_population: preterm infants imaged with brain MRI at term-equivalent age
emb:L2036664225.model_description: Radiomic features were extracted from T1-weighted, T2-weighted and T2-FLAIR brain MRI obtained at term-equivalent age in preterm infants. A classification model combining these radiomic features with perinatal clinical variables was trained to predict motor developmental delay, defined using Bayley Scales assessment at 12-24 months corrected age, and compared to a clinical-variables-only model.
emb:L2036664225.dataset_size: 218 preterm infants (90 with motor developmental delay)
emb:L2036664225.headline_result: AUC for the combined radiomics + clinical model was 0.94 versus 0.87 for the clinical-only model and up to 0.85 for radiomics from combined MRI sequences alone.

emb:L2036545531.model_family: machine learning brain-age estimation model (377 neuroanatomical features from structural MRI)
emb:L2036545531.clinical_problem: brain age gap as a biomarker of anorexia nervosa's effect on brain structure
emb:L2036545531.patient_population: female patients aged 10-40 years with acute or weight-restored anorexia nervosa and age-matched healthy controls
emb:L2036545531.model_description: A machine learning model was trained on 3,487 healthy-control T1-weighted MRI scans (ages 5-45, ten datasets) using 377 neuroanatomical features to estimate brain age. It was then applied to structural MRI from acute anorexia nervosa, weight-restored anorexia nervosa, and matched healthy-control groups from two institutions to compute the brain-predicted age difference (brain-PAD) as a biomarker of accelerated brain aging.
emb:L2036545531.dataset_size: acute AN n=113, weight-restored AN n=35, healthy controls n=90 (model trained on 3,487 healthy-control scans)
emb:L2036545531.headline_result: Model mean absolute error was 2.37 years in healthy controls; brain age was overestimated by 2.25 years in acute AN, normalizing after weight restoration (difference from HC not significant, P=0.98); brain-PAD correlated with BMI in acute AN (r=-0.291, P=0.005).

emb:L2036531047.model_family: segmentation pipeline: ROI detection network + foundation model instance translation + instance classifier network, with curriculum learning
emb:L2036531047.clinical_problem: automated bone segmentation for pediatric bone analysis across ages
emb:L2036531047.patient_population: children aged 4 to 228 months undergoing hand radiography
emb:L2036531047.model_description: PedVision is a segmentation pipeline for hand X-rays that first localizes regions of interest, then uses a foundation model to translate each region into instance-level candidates, which an instance classifier network maps to one of 19 bones across five classes. A semi-automated, foundation-model-assisted annotation workflow with iterative human-in-the-loop review builds the training data across successive rounds, avoiding fully manual annotation, and is designed to scale across a wide pediatric age range including low-quality images.
emb:L2036531047.release_evidence: "The project is open source at github.com/mohofar/PedVision."
emb:L2036531047.dataset_size: hand X-ray images from children aged 4-228 months, segmenting 19 bones into 5 classes (exact image count not stated)
emb:L2036531047.headline_result: Compared with DeepLabV3+ (ResNet34/ResNet101 backbones), the pipeline improved Dice scores by up to 6.19% in subjects over 14 years and 17.01% in subjects under 7 years, particularly in low-quality images.
emb:L2036531047.study_design: technical development / retrospective segmentation accuracy study

emb:L2037149094.clinical_problem: characterizing individual variability of brain functional organization during early adolescent development
emb:L2037149094.patient_population: early adolescents from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, followed over a four-year developmental period
emb:L2037149094.model_description: Metric-BoIT is a deep metric learning model trained on resting-state fMRI functional connectivity data to generate individual 'brain fingerprints.' It was used to identify individuals from their fMRI scans within a single session and up to four years later, and the regions and cognitive/genetic correlates driving these fingerprints were analyzed.
emb:L2037149094.dataset_size: resting-state fMRI from the ABCD dataset (exact n not stated)
emb:L2037149094.headline_result: Individual identification accuracy reached 97.6% within a single session and 86.6% across a four-year developmental period; fingerprints correlated with fluid and crystallized intelligence and with genetic relatedness.

emb:L2036917606.model_family: machine learning regression model on fMRI aperiodic power-spectrum parameters
emb:L2036917606.clinical_problem: assessing brain maturation and effect of preterm birth using functional MRI
emb:L2036917606.patient_population: neonates (preterm and full-term) from the Developing Human Connectome Project
emb:L2036917606.model_description: Using task-free fMRI from the Developing Human Connectome Project, the aperiodic (non-oscillatory) parameters of the BOLD signal power spectrum were extracted from cortical/subcortical regions. A machine learning regression model using aperiodic parameters from 90 brain regions of interest was trained to predict post-menstrual age and postnatal age, and associations with preterm birth were examined.
emb:L2036917606.dataset_size: Developing Human Connectome Project neonatal fMRI cohort (exact n not stated)
emb:L2036917606.headline_result: The regression model predicted post-menstrual and postnatal age with mean test R² of 0.20-0.41; clear differences in aperiodic parameters were found between preterm and full-term infants and between sexes.

emb:L2036917803.model_family: K-means clustering on radiomic features with elastic net logistic regression
emb:L2036917803.clinical_problem: linking imaging appearance to molecular subtype in pediatric low-grade glioma
emb:L2036917803.patient_population: pediatric patients with low-grade glioma (pLGG) from the Children's Brain Tumor Network
emb:L2036917803.model_description: 881 radiomic features plus clinical variables (age, sex, tumor location) were extracted from MRI of pediatric low-grade glioma and grouped into three imaging clusters using principal component analysis and K-means clustering. A supervised elastic net logistic regression model, informed by gene set enrichment and co-expression pathway analysis, was used to link each imaging cluster to specific molecular/transcriptomic pathways and mutation status (e.g., BRAF V600E, KIAA1549::BRAF fusion).
emb:L2036917803.dataset_size: 201 pediatric low-grade glioma patients (Children's Brain Tumor Network)
emb:L2036917803.headline_result: Three distinct imaging clusters were identified with model AUCs of 0.77, 0.78 and 0.70 for the three molecular subtypes; BRAF V600E mutations clustered mainly in imaging cluster 3 and KIAA1549::BRAF fusion in cluster 1.

emb:L2037147915.exclusion_reason: uses wearable accelerometer and temperature sensor data to study fetal activity and infant sleep; not a radiology imaging study

emb:L2036242142.model_name: FNB-ADS (Fetal Nasal Bone Automated Diagnostic System)
emb:L2036242142.model_family: YOLOv8 detection + lightweight segmentation network + ResNet34 classifier
emb:L2036242142.clinical_problem: early prenatal screening for fetal nasal bone abnormality (chromosomal abnormality marker)
emb:L2036242142.patient_population: fetuses undergoing early prenatal mid-sagittal ultrasound screening
emb:L2036242142.model_description: FNB-ADS is an automated pipeline for early-pregnancy fetal nasal bone ultrasound. It uses YOLOv8 to localize the nasal bone region on mid-sagittal plane images, a lightweight segmentation network to segment the nasal bone, nasal tip and prenasal skin, and a ResNet34 classifier to diagnose developmental abnormalities from the segmented structures. The authors also released the FNB-UDV dataset of annotated images and videos used to develop and test the system.
emb:L2036242142.release_evidence: The FNB-UDV image/video dataset is stated to be publicly released, but the abstract does not say whether the model code or weights are released.
emb:L2036242142.dataset_size: 1,007 2D ultrasound images and 12 ultrasound videos (FNB-UDV dataset)
emb:L2036242142.headline_result: Diagnostic accuracy was 92.37% on images (0.14 s/image) and 98.69% on video (0.37 s/frame inference speed).
emb:L2036242142.study_design: technical development / retrospective diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2036917369.model_family: self-supervised deep contrastive learning foundation model
emb:L2036917369.body_region: chest and abdomen (neonatal intensive care radiographs)
emb:L2036917369.clinical_problem: interpretation of neonatal intensive care radiographs (multiple pathologies and device placement)
emb:L2036917369.patient_population: infants who received a radiograph while admitted to a large neonatal intensive care unit
emb:L2036917369.model_description: NeoCLIP is a self-supervised contrastive learning model trained on neonatal intensive care radiographs paired with findings automatically extracted from radiology reports using a large-language-model-based pipeline. It identifies 15 pathologies and 5 medical devices relevant to neonatal intensive care from a plain radiograph, with an option to incorporate patient demographics.
emb:L2036917369.dataset_size: 20,154 radiographs and 15,795 reports from 4,629 infants (3,731 training, 419 validation, 479 test)
emb:L2036917369.headline_result: NeoCLIP's AUROC exceeded all baseline methods for every radiographic finding except portal venous gas, and outperformed similar models developed for adult populations; adding demographics improved AUROC without reaching statistical significance.

emb:L2036213479.model_family: graph-theory connectivity coupling metrics with regression models
emb:L2036213479.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive outcome after pediatric traumatic brain injury
emb:L2036213479.patient_population: children with traumatic brain injury (aged 9-18 years) and healthy controls
emb:L2036213479.model_description: Structural and functional brain connectivity were derived from MRI using graph theory in children with traumatic brain injury and healthy controls, scanned in the acute and post-acute phases. A 'coupling connectivity' measure (correlation between structural and functional graph-theory metrics) was calculated, and regression models used acute-phase coupling connectivity to predict post-acute executive function test outcomes.
emb:L2036213479.dataset_size: 45 children with TBI and 47 healthy controls, aged 9-18 years
emb:L2036213479.headline_result: TBI patients showed disrupted structural-functional connectivity coupling versus controls, and acute-phase coupling connectivity significantly predicted post-acute executive function outcomes.

emb:L2036917276.model_family: deep learning classification model (architecture not specified)
emb:L2036917276.clinical_problem: detection of childhood pneumonia on chest radiographs in a low-resource setting
emb:L2036917276.patient_population: children in Nigeria undergoing chest radiography, prospectively sampled across two radiology departments
emb:L2036917276.model_description: An AI model was developed on an open-source US pediatric chest radiograph dataset to classify images as normal or pneumonia, then externally tested on prospectively collected Nigerian pediatric chest radiographs read by two blinded radiologists as the reference standard, to evaluate generalizability to a low-resource clinical setting.
emb:L2036917276.dataset_size: 5,232 open-source pediatric chest radiographs for development (1,349 normal/3,883 pneumonia training; 234/390 internal test) and 190 Nigerian radiographs for external testing (93 normal/97 pneumonia)
emb:L2036917276.headline_result: The model achieved 86% accuracy and 0.93 AUC on the internal test set, but only 58% accuracy and 0.65 AUC on the external Nigerian test set.

emb:L2037147257.exclusion_reason: computational/theoretical fMRI study of visual cortex development after transient neonatal cataracts, using a deep neural network only as a modeling analogy; participant age at scanning and pediatric status are not stated

emb:L2034303818.model_family: Optimized Pyramidal Convolution Shuffle Attention Neural Network
emb:L2034303818.clinical_problem: identifying end-systolic and end-diastolic cardiac cycle frames on fetal echocardiography
emb:L2034303818.patient_population: fetuses undergoing echocardiography (Shenzhen Maternal and Child Health Hospital)
emb:L2034303818.model_description: OPCSANN-FCCD detects the end-systolic and end-diastolic frames within fetal echocardiogram video clips, a step needed for automated cardiac biometric assessment. Ultrasound frames are first denoised with an anisotropic diffusion filter, texture features are extracted with a window-adaptive gray-level co-occurrence matrix, and a pyramidal convolution shuffle-attention neural network classifies frames as end-systolic or end-diastolic.
emb:L2034303818.dataset_size: Shenzhen Maternal and Child Health Hospital fetal echocardiogram dataset (exact n not stated)
emb:L2034303818.headline_result: OPCSANN-FCCD improved accuracy by 22.4-27.6% and reduced computational load by 26.6-31.2% compared with three existing fetal cardiac-cycle detection methods (FCCD-ME-HCF, FCUSD-ML-MAM, HFSCCD-UV).

emb:L2035228739.exclusion_reason: narrative review of fetal cognition and consciousness drawing on behavioral, animal and neuroimaging evidence broadly; not focused on an AI/ML imaging model

emb:L2036436001.clinical_problem: improving image quality of affordable ultra-low-field brain MRI for pediatric neuroimaging
emb:L2036436001.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing ultra-low-field brain MRI
emb:L2036436001.model_description: A deep learning model generates a super-resolved brain MRI from a single ultra-low-field scan, without requiring paired high-field training data or the three orthogonal ultra-low-field acquisitions used by prior multi-resolution registration methods. Output quality was assessed by image quality metrics, correlation of derived tissue volumes, and Dice overlap of tissue segmentations, including an exploratory test of generalization across scanning sites.
emb:L2036436001.headline_result: The single-scan deep learning approach significantly improved image quality metrics, tissue volume correlations, and Dice overlap of tissue segmentations compared with the single ultra-low-field input; an exploratory external site evaluation suggested site-specific retraining may be needed to address domain shift.

emb:L2032278003.model_family: deep learning bone age prediction model
emb:L2032278003.clinical_problem: bone age assessment in children from different ethnicities and altitudes
emb:L2032278003.patient_population: children undergoing left-hand radiography, including Han and Tibetan children from plain and highland regions
emb:L2032278003.model_description: EVG-BANet is a deep learning model that predicts bone age from a left-hand radiograph. It was trained on the public RSNA and RHPE bone-age datasets plus a self-established dataset of Han and Tibetan children from a plain-region and a highland-region hospital, then evaluated on an independent external test set of Tibetan children from a third hospital.
emb:L2032278003.dataset_size: RSNA dataset (train 12,611/val 1,425/test 200), RHPE dataset (train 5,491/val 713/test 79), self-established dataset (train 825/test 351 from 1,176 children), external test 256 children
emb:L2032278003.headline_result: Mean absolute difference from reference bone age ranged 0.34-0.53 years and accuracy within 1 year ranged 89.45%-97.72% across the RSNA, RHPE, self-established, and external test sets.
emb:L2032278003.study_design: retrospective multi-center diagnostic accuracy / external validation study

emb:L2035838150.exclusion_reason: AI model uses 12-lead/single-lead ECG signals to classify cardiac dysfunction, not imaging

emb:L2036294221.model_family: DenseNet121 and YOLOv8 convolutional neural networks
emb:L2036294221.clinical_problem: identifying technically suboptimal chest radiographs to reduce repeat imaging
emb:L2036294221.patient_population: patients undergoing chest radiography, median age 67 years (range 0-102), including pediatric and adult cases
emb:L2036294221.model_description: DenseNet121 and YOLOv8 convolutional neural networks were trained to classify chest radiographs (both PA and lateral views) as optimal or suboptimal quality, a task intended to flag images likely to need repeat acquisition. Model classifications were compared with radiologists' classifications, and this was the first such study to include lateral views and pediatric cases.
emb:L2036294221.dataset_size: 3,587 patients; 10,000 CXRs total (4,000/4,000 training, 400/400 validation, 25/25 test)
emb:L2036294221.headline_result: DenseNet121 achieved AUROC 0.97 and YOLOv8 AUROC 0.95 for distinguishing optimal from suboptimal chest radiographs; agreement with radiologists varied but differences were not statistically significant.

emb:L2030471497.clinical_problem: deciding whether tube thoracostomy is needed for pediatric pneumothorax or pleural effusion
emb:L2030471497.patient_population: pediatric patients admitted between 2005 and 2022 with pneumothorax or pleural effusion
emb:L2030471497.model_description: XRAInet is a deep learning decision-support system trained on chest X-rays to identify pediatric patients with pneumothorax or pleural effusion and to localize the abnormal region, supporting the decision of whether tube thoracostomy intervention is warranted versus conservative management.
emb:L2030471497.headline_result: XRAInet achieved a mean average precision of 0.918; on an independent test set, sensitivity was 64.00% and specificity was 96.15%.

emb:L2033942572.exclusion_reason: uses non-contact pose estimation from photographs/video, not a radiology imaging modality

emb:L2036230564.exclusion_reason: review of ChatGPT/LLM chatbot applications across obstetric practice (patient education, drug counseling, administration); imaging is a brief tangential mention, not the focus

emb:L2035580871.exclusion_reason: external validation of a multimodal clinical prediction model for pediatric appendicitis using demographic, clinical, laboratory and scoring data; ultrasound is only one of several non-imaging inputs, not an imaging-centric AI model

emb:L2035580700.exclusion_reason: population age is not stated; uses a general public chest X-ray pneumonia dataset without confirming a pediatric cohort

emb:L2035793475.model_family: Graph Neural Network trained on Ising-model networks
emb:L2035793475.clinical_problem: characterizing brain functional maturation using resting-state fMRI
emb:L2035793475.patient_population: typically developing children and children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
emb:L2035793475.model_description: A Graph Neural Network trained on simulated 2D Ising-model networks was used to estimate an 'Ising temperature' from resting-state fMRI functional connectivity, a marker of how close brain dynamics are to a critical state. The method was applied to children to study how this measure changes with age in typical development and in ADHD.
emb:L2035793475.headline_result: Ising temperature correlated negatively with age in both typically developing children (r=-0.48, P<0.0001) and children with ADHD (r=-0.49, P<0.0001), suggesting the brain moves away from criticality with age.

emb:L2035579909.clinical_problem: computer-aided detection of tuberculosis on chest radiographs in children
emb:L2035579909.patient_population: children evaluated for tuberculosis with chest radiography, particularly in primary health settings
emb:L2035579909.model_description: This review summarizes the current, limited literature on computer-aided detection (CAD) algorithms for reading chest radiographs to diagnose tuberculosis and other pulmonary infections in children, noting that CAD systems approved for adult TB triage are not yet approved for pediatric use, and calling for large, diverse, well-annotated pediatric chest radiograph datasets to train or fine-tune such models.

emb:L2026785820.model_family: artificial intelligence Greulich-Pyle (GP) bone age assessment system (domestically developed)
emb:L2026785820.clinical_problem: bone age assessment using the Greulich-Pyle method
emb:L2026785820.patient_population: children and adolescents aged 6-15 years undergoing wrist radiography
emb:L2026785820.model_description: A domestically developed AI system that applies the Greulich-Pyle atlas method to wrist radiographs was compared against manual GP bone-age assessment by an expert, in a cohort of boys and girls aged 6-15 years, to check whether the AI system's readings agree closely enough with expert readings for clinical use.
emb:L2026785820.dataset_size: 1,322 wrist radiographs from children/adolescents 6-15 years (672 male, 650 female)
emb:L2026785820.headline_result: Mean absolute difference from expert GP assessment was 0.39 years (male) and 0.32 years (female); Pearson correlation r=0.991 (male) and r=0.992 (female); overall Kappa 0.603 (male) and 0.659 (female).

emb:L2031524570.exclusion_reason: scoping review of digital technology in pediatric dentistry (dental imaging, CAD/CAM, teledentistry); dental imaging is out of scope

emb:L2031545615.exclusion_reason: population age not stated; uses a general public chest X-ray dataset (Mendeley) without confirming a pediatric cohort, despite background mention of children

emb:L2034988949.clinical_problem: landscape of AI applications across pediatric radiology
emb:L2034988949.model_description: This systematic review, following PRISMA and Cochrane Collaboration guidance, surveys AI research in pediatric radiology published from 2015 to 2021, covering use cases, tasks, methodologies, and underlying data. It reports the distribution of subspecialties, imaging modalities, tasks, and study designs, and highlights potential biases and data-quality issues limiting generalizability.
emb:L2034988949.headline_result: 292 articles were included with an increasing annual publication trend; neuroradiology and musculoskeletal radiology were the most common subspecialties, MRI was the dominant modality, and segmentation and classification were the most common tasks, with retrospective cohort studies predominating.

emb:L2034696700.exclusion_reason: review comparing international clinical guidelines for fetal growth restriction (definitions, screening, genetic counseling, monitoring, delivery timing); AI/multi-omics is a brief tangential mention, not the subject of review

emb:L2034988463.model_family: vision transformer (pretrained on ImageNet, fine-tuned) with age-fusion; convolutional network compared
emb:L2034988463.clinical_problem: classification of pediatric brain tumor type
emb:L2034988463.patient_population: pediatric patients with low-grade astrocytoma, ependymoma, or medulloblastoma from the Children's Brain Tumor Network (age range 0.01-36.49 years)
emb:L2034988463.model_description: Deep learning models were trained to classify pediatric brain tumor type (low-grade astrocytoma, ependymoma, medulloblastoma) from transversal MRI slices showing tumor, using T1-weighted post-contrast, T2-weighted, or ADC sequences separately. Patient age was fused with image features (joint fusion), and two pre-training strategies were compared; Grad-CAM and PCA were used to visualize model attention and the learned feature space.
emb:L2034988463.dataset_size: 178 subjects (T1w post-contrast n=94, T2w n=160, ADC n=66) from the Children's Brain Tumor Network
emb:L2034988463.headline_result: The best model (vision transformer pretrained on ImageNet, fine-tuned on ADC images with age fusion) achieved MCC 0.77±0.14 and accuracy 0.87±0.08, outperforming models trained on T2w (MCC 0.58) and T1w post-contrast (MCC 0.41) data.
emb:L2034988463.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2031408230.model_family: statistical and machine learning prediction models
emb:L2031408230.clinical_problem: early prediction of autism spectrum disorder from prenatal and early postnatal brain imaging
emb:L2031408230.patient_population: fetuses (via prenatal ultrasound) and their offspring followed postnatally with MRI at 6 and 12 months
emb:L2031408230.model_description: In a prospective cohort of pregnant women and their offspring, fetal head circumference, corpus callosum thickness and ventricle size were assessed with 3D/4D ultrasound, and postnatal brain structure (amygdala size, frontal cortical volume) was assessed with MRI at 6 and 12 months. Statistical tests and machine learning algorithms were used to evaluate how well these prenatal and postnatal imaging markers predicted later autism spectrum disorder diagnosis.
emb:L2031408230.headline_result: Prediction accuracy for autism spectrum disorder was 70% using antenatal ultrasound alone, 85% using postnatal MRI alone, and 90% combining both.

emb:L2030745588.clinical_problem: AI applications in pediatric urologic imaging (vesicoureteral reflux grading, hydronephrosis, bladder dysfunction)
emb:L2030745588.patient_population: pediatric patients with vesicoureteral reflux, hydronephrosis, or lower urinary tract dysfunction
emb:L2030745588.model_description: This review surveys existing and emerging AI models in pediatric urology, including machine learning and deep learning approaches for grading vesicoureteral reflux, explainable models predicting obstructive hydronephrosis from ultrasound images alone, and ensemble models integrating video urodynamic pressure tracings with fluoroscopic images to characterize bladder dysfunction, while noting persistent problems with generalizability, transparency and reproducibility.

emb:L2032329782.clinical_problem: detection of primary brain tumors in children
emb:L2032329782.patient_population: pediatric patients with primary brain tumors imaged at King Abdullah Specialist Children's Hospital
emb:L2032329782.model_description: MRI images of pediatric patients with primary brain tumors (glioma, primitive neuro-ectodermal tumor, pituitary tumor) and normal images were retrieved from the hospital's PACS. Machine learning algorithms, including an artificial neural network, were trained on 70% of the images and tested on the remaining 30% to classify and detect brain tumors.
emb:L2032329782.headline_result: The artificial neural network method accurately detected pediatric primary brain tumors, with results reported to match the radiologist's report (no single summary accuracy figure given).
